title: Short cutover ops playbook and annotated release notes (Mar 2026)
body:
Purpose and scope:
This doc is a compact, executable playbook for a short-cutover release (target window: 90–150 minutes) covering preflight checks, minute-by-minute cutover calendar, rollback matrix, and an annotated draft of release notes for engineering and on-call teams. Intended audience: release engineer on duty (RED), service owners, SRE on-call, product manager, and solutions eng.

High-level objective:
- Deploy service changes to hosted API and Dedicated orchestration with minimal customer-visible disruption.
- Keep the window <= 2.5 hours; safe rollback target: full restore within 30 minutes of a rollback decision.

Preflight (T-72h to T-1h) checklist:
- T-72h: Code and infra PRs merged to release branch, tags created, upgrade smoke tests green (owner: feature leads).
- T-48h: Run full e2e smoke on staging (sequence length, batching, streaming). Attach logs to REL-1423 (owner: QA).
- T-48h: Confirm migration plan for KV-cache compatibility and model variant mapping; mark any incompatible model versions in the catalog (owner: serving-runtime).
- T-24h: Canary plan reviewed and approved by RED and SRE; traffic split strategy defined (owner: RED).
- T-12h: Whitelist maintenance windows in cloud accounts, ensure RBAC for deploy runbooks (owner: infra).
- T-4h: Nightly metrics snapshot (latency P50/P95/P99, cost per 1k tokens, QPS) exported to release folder (owner: observability).
- T-2h: Notify customers on the scheduled window (outbound email, dashboard banner) and internal slack #prod-release (owner: customer-success/product-comms).
- T-1h: Final health checks: disk, GPU memory, connection pools, KMS connectivity; confirm backups for feature flags and routing policies (owner: SRE).

Cutover calendar (minute-level plan) – target 10:00–11:40 UTC (example)
- 10:00 – 10:05: Kickoff: RED confirms all participants on call, recording started, communication channels pinned.
- 10:05 – 10:15: Snapshot current infra state: cluster autoscaler status, node counts, running model-serving pods (owner: infra).
- 10:15 – 10:25: Deploy infra YAML (scalable pools) and rollout model binary to canary nodes (5% traffic).
- 10:25 – 10:40: Run a scripted set of smoke prompts against canary endpoints (latency, token accuracy checks) and run eval probes (owner: QA, applied-ml).
- 10:40 – 10:50: Review canary metrics; if green, increase canary to 30% (owner: RED).
- 10:50 – 11:05: Monitor stability windows; run long-sequence batch jobs to watch memory/KV-sync behavior (owner: SRE).
- 11:05 – 11:15: Gradual ramp to 100% across routing policy (region-by-region over 5 min each) with automated rollback hooks enabled.
- 11:15 – 11:30: Post-rollout sanity checks: business-critical synthetic flows, ingestion pipelines, storage latencies (owner: service owners).
- 11:30 – 11:40: Close window: announce success or trigger rollback. If rollback, notify stakeholders and execute rollback matrix.

Rollout decision criteria (green if all true):
- Canary latency P95 <= baseline P95 + 50ms for 15 minutes.
- Error rate <= baseline error rate + 0.2% sustained for 10 minutes.
- No increase in cache eviction rate or KV-mismatch incidents.
- No regressions on core eval prompt set (0.5% tolerance).

Rollback matrix (fast paths and responsibilities):
- Class A (showstopper customer-facing errors: high error rate, auth failures): Immediate rollback to previous stable tag. RED executes rollback script, infra scales down new pods, tag reverts, routing policy restored (target RTO: 15–30m). Notify execs and CS.
- Class B (performance regression: P95 degrade > 150ms): Pause ramp, throttle traffic to older variant, roll back model binary for affected region only (target RTO: 30–45m).
- Class C (noncritical feature regression or cosmetic): Freeze rollout, hotfix PR if trivial; otherwise schedule next patch cycle.

Rollback playbook steps (scripted):
1) Stop traffic to new variant (RED).
2) Run controlled replacement: kubectl rollouts undo deployment/<svc> --to-revision=<prev> (infra).
3) Validate health (SRE runs fast checks).
4) Reopen full traffic only after 3 consecutive 5-min windows green.
5) Create post-rollback ticket with CRITICAL label and start immediate RCA if user impact > 1% or > 10 enterprise customers.

Monitoring and dashboards to watch (alerts and runbooks):
- api-latency-p95-prod (dashboard: releases/latency-overview)
- streaming-token-error-count (alerts: alert/streaming-errors)
- kv-sync-failures (alert/kv-sync)
- gpu-memory-pressure (alert/gpu-oom)
- per-route error breakdown (dashboard: per-route-health)
- billing spike detection: token-usage anomaly (alert/cost-anomaly)
Assign on-call pairs for each alert; list of SMEs pinned in Slack channel #release-ops.

Communication plan (who says what):
- Before window: banner on status.redwood.ai and email to customers with >1% usage. (owner: CS)
- During window: Slack channel #prod-release for internal updates; update release ticket every 15 min (owner: RED).
- After window: Short post to #all-hands with success summary and link to release notes (owner: product-comms).

Post-release validation (first 24h):
- 0–2h: High-frequency synthetic checks for endpoints and embedding pipelines.
- 2–6h: Run stochastic evals across production prompts; compare to baseline; flag regressions > 1%.
- 6–24h: Cost delta review (tokens/unit + GPU-hours) and log-sampling for subtle errors.
- If any major regression appears, escalate per SLO incident runbook.

Annotated release notes (engineering draft) – for internal + external consumption:
Title: Short-cutover: improved routing resilience and KV-cache sync fixes (Mar 2026)
Overview: This release includes two primary changes targeted at reducing tail latency and improving cache consistency during model rollouts. It also contains a small set of developer-facing improvements to our deployment orchestration.
Highlights (customer-facing bullets):
- Reduced tail latency on text-generation endpoints by optimizing kernel selection for medium-length sequences (expected P95 improvement 25–60ms).
- Fixed KV-cache sync issue that could occasionally cause stale completions for long-context prompts.
- Improved rollback safety: routing policy now supports region-scoped rollbacks.
Developer notes (breaking/upgrade items):
- Deprecated: legacy routing flag "route.v1_compat" removed. If you manage private deployments with custom routing, update your rotation config.
- Migration: KV cache metadata schema bumped; private-deploy customers must run the included migration tool (see linked artifact) prior to rollout or the service will reject requests for pinned model versions.
Bug fixes and perf tweaks (short list):
- infra: autoscaler now respects GPU padding rules (fixes sporadic OOM at scale).
- serving-runtime: improved attention kernel fallback for quantized LLaMA variants.
Known issues / caveats:
- Small regression in embedding cosine stability at extremely short vectors (<5 tokens) observed in staging; monitoring in place and under investigation by applied-ml.
- Customers using on-prem edge-packages older than 2.1.4 may need config tweaks — CS will contact impacted accounts.

Post-release actions and tickets to create:
- REL-FOLLOWUP-204: Collect 24h perf snapshot and compare to baseline (owner: observability).
- REL-FOLLOWUP-205: Confirm migration tool docs updated for private deployment customers (owner: private-deployments).
- REL-FOLLOWUP-206: Run regression sweep for embedding short-vector stability (owner: applied-ml).

Notes to self / open questions (work-in-progress):
- Should we include a brief synthetic that simulates multi-tenant KV thrashing to stress test cache invalidation? (QA + applied-ml)
- Can the rollback path be shortened further by pre-loading previous model variants into standby nodes? Cost vs. benefit analysis needed.

Appendix: quick command snippets for RED
- Rollback service: ./scripts/release rollback --service api-gateway --to-tag v1.42.3
- Toggle routing split: ./scripts/traffic set-split --service text-gen --variant stable=70,new=30
- Collect fast logs: ./scripts/logs fetch --since 30m --service serving-runtime | gzip > /tmp/serving-logs.gz

End of doc.

Changelog: initial draft (2026-03-01) by Ava Martinez. Minor edits and canary metrics thresholds tuned by Daniel Kim (2026-03-06). Added annotated release notes and migration reminder (2026-03-10 by Priya Rao).
